title: Emergency Access Users page: statuses, dates and actions

prose.text: The page shows each user's state in the identity provider. {{page-columns}}
Where these users come from and who can see them: [[zpa.emergency-access.identity]] and [[zpa.emergency-access.configuration]]. The same fields through the API: [[zpa.emergency-access.api-surface]].

checks.do: The user's status, and what that status means: whether email authentication has completed.
Activation Date and Last Login Date for evidence the user activated and signed in.

page-columns.statement: The Emergency Access Users page lists First Name, Last Name, Email Address, Status, Activation Date (when the admin activated the user) and Last Login Date.

quotes: **First Name**: The first name of the emergency access user, as provided by the admin.
**Email Address**: The email address of the emergency access user, as provided by the admin.
**Activation Date**: The date and time when the emergency access user was activated by the admin.
**Last Login Date**: The date and time when the emergency access user last logged in.

status-values.statement: The status is Active (activated and email authentication completed), Staged (created in the IdP, neither activated nor deactivated), Provisioned (created and activated, still to complete email authentication), Deprovisioned (created in the IdP but not activated) or Suspended (no access to applications within the IdP).

quotes: **Active**: The user is activated and has completed the email-based authentication.
**Staged**: The user is created in the IdP but neither activated nor deactivated.
**Provisioned**: The user is created and activated in the IdP, but still needs to complete activation via email-based authentication.
**Deprovisioned**: The user is created in the IdP but not activated.
**Suspended**: The user does not have access to applications within the IdP.

other-statuses.statement: Other statuses, such as Password Expired, Locked Out and Recovery, might appear.

quotes: Other statuses (e.g., **Password Expired**, **Locked Out**, **Recovery**) might appear.

page-actions.statement: From the page an emergency access user can be edited, activated and deactivated.

quotes: 7. Edit an emergency access user. 8. Activate an emergency access user. 9. Deactivate an emergency access user.
